title: 第7章 上街诊病赚钱第8章 在何家偶遇大国手苏神医
content_zh:
夜深人静，窗外月光洒落，陈景言睁眼望着帘子缝隙透出的微光，耳边是柳云烟均匀的呼吸声。
这一晚，陈景言似睡非睡，脑海中挥之不去过往的记忆。
在他的记忆里，陈家人对他很好，养父养母，还有他的两个姐姐对他都很好。可他们为什么要把他当成获取利益的工具？
在他回陈家的时候，没有给他一分钱，一套新衣服也不过是地摊货。
吴家那就更不用说了，在吴家人眼中，他就是一个灾星，只会给吴家带来无妄之灾。
柳家也是如此，或许柳家也根本就没有把他当人看待。
第二天一早，陈景言换上从陈家带来的那套地摊货，陪着柳云烟吃早餐。
吃完早餐，柳云烟就去公司了。
陈景言留在柳家，几乎没人在意他的存在。就连佣人都只是匆匆瞥他一眼，便低头绕开。
院子里的花草修剪得整齐，空气里飘着淡淡的桂花香，却没人问他是否需要什么。
快到九点钟了，陈景言实在闲的无聊，他走出柳家庄园。
门口的保安连看都懒得多看他一眼。
陈景言漫无目的地走在街上，看到一个测字算命的摊位，他驻足观看。
摊主是个须发皆白的老者，眼皮耷拉，仿佛睡着。
陈景言蹲下身。
老者睁开眼睛，看了一眼陈景言：“小伙子，你想算什么？”
陈景言没有犹豫就说道：“我不算命，我也想给别人算命。”
老者忍不住笑了起来：“小子，你知不知道，我们这个行业现在有多卷？算命？你也要靠这个混饭吃？真好笑。”
陈景言盯着老者浑浊却锐利的眼睛，忽然咧嘴一笑：“我不怕卷，反正我一无所有。”
他说着，就拿起老者面前的毛笔，蘸墨，在一张黄纸上写上：算命，改命，转运，治疑难杂症，包治百病，童叟无欺。

老者看到陈景言在黄纸上写的字，忍不住哈哈大笑：“小子，你真当自己是神棍？”
陈景言放下笔，拿起纸张，说了声“谢谢”就走了。
老者指着陈景言离去的背影，自言自语：“小神经病。”
陈景言来到另一条街上，摊开纸张，从路边捡来四个石子压住纸张的四个角，蹲在地上开始吆喝。
“算命，看相，治疗各种疑难杂症，治不好不要钱。”
路过的行人纷纷侧目，有人嗤笑，有人驻足观望。
终于有一个老人走到陈景言面前，浑浊的眼睛盯着黄纸上的字看了许久，忽然颤声问：“你真能治病？”
陈景言大声说道：“大爷，医院能治好的病，不用找我，我只治疗医院治不了的疑难杂症。”
“好大的口气，小子，你这话有点托大，你不知道吗？现在的人都变得越来越聪明了，不好骗了。”
老人家说得振振有词。
围观的人越来越多。
机会来了，山潮水潮不如人潮。
content_en:
In the dead of night, with the moonlight shining outside the window, Chen Jingyan opened his eyes and looked at the dim light coming from the gap in the curtain, and heard Liu Yunyan's even breathing in his ears.
That night, Chen Jingyan couldn't sleep, and the memories of the past lingered in his mind.
In his memory, the Chen family was very kind to him, including his adoptive father, his adoptive mother, and his two sisters. But why do they use him as a tool to obtain profits?
When he returned to Chen's house, he was not given a penny, and a new set of clothes was nothing more than street food.
Not to mention the Wu family. In the eyes of the Wu family, he is a disaster star who will only bring unreasonable disasters to the Wu family.
The same was true for the Liu family. Maybe the Liu family didn't treat him as a human being at all.
Early the next morning, Chen Jingyan put on the street stall goods he brought from the Chen family and had breakfast with Liu Yunyan.
After breakfast, Liu Yunyan went to the company.
Chen Jingyan stayed in the Liu family, and almost no one cared about his existence. Even the servants only glanced at him briefly, then lowered their heads and walked away.
The flowers and plants in the yard were neatly trimmed, and there was a faint scent of osmanthus in the air, but no one asked him if he needed anything.
It was almost nine o'clock, and Chen Jingyan was really bored, so he walked out of Liu's Manor.
The security guard at the door didn't even bother to look at him.
Chen Jingyan was walking aimlessly on the street and saw a fortune-telling booth. He stopped to watch.
The stall owner is an old man with white beard and hair. His eyelids are drooped, as if he is asleep.
Chen Jingyan squatted down.
The old man opened his eyes and glanced at Chen Jingyan: "Young man, what do you want to do?"
Chen Jingyan said without hesitation: "I don't tell fortunes, and I also want to tell others' fortunes."
The old man couldn't help but laugh: "Boy, do you know how many fortune-telling companies there are in our industry now? Do you have to rely on this to earn a living? It's really funny."
Chen Jingyan stared at the old man's cloudy but sharp eyes, and suddenly grinned: "I'm not afraid of curling up, I have nothing anyway."
As he spoke, he picked up the brush in front of the old man, dipped it in ink, and wrote on a piece of yellow paper: fortune telling, fortune changing, fortune-telling, treatment of difficult and complicated diseases, cure for all diseases, no deception.
When the old man saw what Chen Jingyan wrote on the yellow paper, he couldn't help laughing: "Boy, do you really think you are a magic stick?"
Chen Jingyan put down his pen, picked up the paper, said "thank you" and left.
The old man pointed at Chen Jingyan's leaving figure and muttered to himself: "Little lunatic."
Chen Jingyan came to another street, spread out the paper, picked up four stones from the roadside, pressed the four corners of the paper, squatted on the ground and started shouting.
"Fortune telling, fortune telling, and treatment of all kinds of difficult and complicated diseases. If you can't cure it, you don't have to pay for it."
Pedestrians passing by looked sideways, some sneered, and some stopped to watch.
Finally, an old man walked up to Chen Jingyan. He stared at the words on the yellow paper with his cloudy eyes for a long time, and suddenly asked in a trembling voice: "Can you really cure diseases?"
Chen Jingyan said loudly: "Uncle, you don't need to come to me for diseases that the hospital can cure. I only treat difficult and complicated diseases that the hospital can't cure."
"What a big tone, kid. What you said is a bit exaggerated. Don't you know? People are getting smarter and smarter now, and it's hard to lie to them."
The old man spoke plausibly.
More and more people are watching.
When the opportunity comes, the tide of mountains and rivers is not as good as the tide of people.
